question.worked_solution:
Using the adjacent intervals rule, we have

$$
{\int }_{1}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t={\int }_{1}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{3}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

We can rearrange the above as follows:

$$
{\int }_{1}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t={\int }_{1}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{3}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Finally, using the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{3}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{5}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,-3⟩+⟨-1,\,2,\,-7⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,4,\,-10⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
